summary: Scope. Trial 2 of the continuous performance campaign, on top of trial-1-optimized main (fc670da). Four lanes across two waves: interface startup, decode CPU, download orchestration, RAM/storage — every change measured on this machine, every rejection documented with the numbers that killed it.

What improved. Every CLI invocation now starts at the bare-node floor (33.2→24.5 ms) via lazy per-command loading. Manifest hashing no longer pumps a fresh buffered stream per file: each of 8 workers reuses one 1 MiB buffer over an explicit pread loop — 51.6→32.2 ms on a 50 MB many-file tree (−38%), 272.2→147.5 ms at 200 MB (−46%), and −20% (20.71→16.47 ms) on a single 50 MB blob, outputs byte-identical everywhere.

What was measured and left alone. archive --all loan pipelining (saves exactly (N−1)×setup: 1.24× on a fast-download sim, only 2.2% on a 4-loan local e2e — single-digit % of real walls; a round-1 cross-loan corruption bug found in hostile review stands as the complexity tax; code preserved, not adopted). cfc1’s u32 swap (1.60× isolated, ~1% e2e — the 19 ms bench headline was a random-bytes utf8 artifact; realistic pages decode in 3.4 ms). Manifest hwm/worker knobs (both neutral-to-worse). EPUB assembly RAM is already within ~12 MB of the theory floor (transient allocator churn, not retention). Cover buffering and sidecar JSON format: below the worth-it bar.

State. Checkpoint, not closed: branch perf-trial-20260909 carries two adopted wins (5fe5d0b W1A, 06d6320 W2D) plus evidence commits; tests 80/80 after the reconciliation commit reverted the un-adopted W2C bundle off the adoptable line (preserved at e2b920d / branch perf-trial-20260909-035217 / perf/lanes/T2-W2C-alt/). Meta verification bench: perf/results-meta-verify.json. Open owner decisions: issues #2 (pipelining latency trade) and the storage questions below.

Owner decision implemented (T2-W3). Readable archives are now EPUB-only: the decoded pages, their image assets, and the cover live only inside the EPUB — assets and cover byte-identical, page bodies embedded verbatim in the reader-required XHTML shell. Payloads stage in a per-run temp dir during assembly, so the memory profile is unchanged; the finished folder carries ~half the bytes (45 MB magazine: ~88 → ~43 MB).

waves.name: CLI startup — lazy per-command loading
waves.change: bin/libby.mjs statically imported all 12 src modules (including the heavy archive/EPUB/openbook/read subgraph) before dispatching any command. Now a `load` map of lazy import() arrows resolves only what the invoked command needs; SentryError is lazy-imported at its 3 catch sites; the COMMANDS/unknown gate still runs before any import. Output text, exit codes, and error behavior byte-identical (diffed against the pre-change binary for help/where/probe/unknown).
tradeoffs: ~0.05–0.3 ms warm import cost added per command dispatch (net win everywhere; `where` only −2.1 ms because config.mjs itself pulls sentry+http — a config-module split would be needed for more)
typo risk in the command→module map — pinned by new test/cli-lazy.test.mjs (usage table covers COMMANDS exactly; every command's loaders resolve to the exact functions its branch destructures)
`where` still pays for https agents at import; left alone deliberately (splitting config.mjs churns the public API for ~2 ms)
waves.verified: npm test 80 pass / 0 fail (78 baseline + 2 new); coordinator re-measured help 26.2 ms; commit 5fe5d0b

waves.name: cfc1 page-blob decode — word-at-a-time quad swap
waves.change: Built and verified a u32 word-trick swap (view+shift/mask, plus 3 other variants) with byte-identical output on 144 adversarial fixtures (terminators at every offset, pairs gap 0..7, lengths incl. n%4!=0, U+2029 fallback path — the harness even caught a wrong-top-byte bug in the first draft before timing). Verdict: the isolated swap loop runs 1.60x faster (0.533→0.334 ms on 2.8 MB), but the swap is ~3% of the decode pipeline, so end-to-end the best variant manages only 1.01x (random blob) / 1.08x (realistic XHTML) — far under the 15% bar. Not adopted; src/read.mjs untouched; the 6-line change is documented as adopted-ready.
tradeoffs: Key finding: the bench headline cfc1 number (19.4 ms) is a fixture artifact — random base64 bytes force Node’s error-tolerant slow utf8 decode, 95% of runtime; realistic ASCII page content decodes in ~3.4 ms where the swap matters even less
Stage split: base64 ≈ 0.3 ms; utf8 toString dominates random bytes; TextDecoder is identical — no remaining lever in this pipeline worth a wave
Rejected variants recorded so the next trial never re-runs them: u16 halfword pairs, unrolled byte loop, readUInt32LE/writeUInt32LE (0.15x — method-call overhead)
waves.verified: npm test 80 pass / 0 fail; git diff confirms src/ untouched; evidence in perf/loop-showdown.mjs T2 section + perf-notes-t2-loops.md

waves.name: archive --all loan pipelining + read-path manifest pre-hash
waves.change: (1) Loan pipelining: archiveAudiobook/archiveReadable split into prepareX (claim folder + open loan + decode openbook — REST round trips) and finishX (downloads + assembly); archiveLoanQueue in bin keeps exactly ONE next-loan setup in flight during the active loan’s downloads. Prefetched logs buffer and replay in loan order (transcript-equality test), a failed prefetch surfaces as that loan’s FAILED line, whoa still exits 3, and the composed single-loan exports are preserved for the library API. (2) Read-path pre-hash: page bodies, assets, and the cover are sha256-hashed as they are written and fed to writeManifest’s known map alongside the EPUB digest, so the integrity pass re-reads only small sidecars; resume stays correct because only files written this run get entries.

writeManifest on 16.1 MB / 222 files, all pre-hashed (median of 5)

tradeoffs: META RULING (reconciliation): adoption DECLINED — the saving is fixed at (N−1)×setup time, so its share of wall collapses to single digits against real download-dominated archives; the hostile-review round-1 cross-loan corruption bug stands as the complexity tax. Code preserved: history commit e2b920d, branch perf-trial-20260909-035217, receipt/notes in perf/lanes/T2-W2C-alt/. The read-path pre-hash sub-part is pattern-consistent with W17/W18 and available for separate adoption if the owner unbundles it.
pipelining only saves the LAST setup round trips × (N−1) — real-world ~0.2–0.6 s per loan given gateway RTTs; wall-clock is still dominated by downloads
one extra setup’s REST traffic may be wasted if the run whoa-exits before that loan becomes active (teardown on exit; acceptable, bounded to one loan)
the pre-hash win is re-read avoidance (files are warm in page cache just after writing) — the hashing work itself moves into the download phase rather than disappearing
prepare/finish is a public-API addition (additive exports; existing signatures unchanged) — noted for semver

HONEST MAGNITUDE (coordinator correction after cross-checking a second, independently built implementation of this wave): the win is latency-dependent — +24% on the large-scale sim (60 ms setup RTT, 400 ms parts) but only +2.2% on a small-scale 4-loan e2e sim (see perf/lanes/T2-W2C-alt/). Real-world expectation: single-digit % of wall; it saves (N−1) setup round trips (~0.5–3 s each), which is small next to minutes of downloading

complexity tax is real: the alternative implementation in the alt lane had a consumed-prefetch state leak (cross-loan sidecar mixing) found by hostile review — this implementation is structured differently (each prefetch is a self-contained setup object; pending is cleared every iteration) and its order/failure contracts are pinned by test/archive-pipeline.test.mjs; coordinator traced the leak path as absent here
the alt lane’s implementation was measured-rejected under a 10% bar and lives only as evidence in perf/lanes/T2-W2C-alt/ (receipt + notes + its regression test)

waves.name: EPUB assembly RAM/storage audit on big fixtures
waves.change: RATIFIED by the meta-coordinator after independent reproduction (single 50 MB blob 20.71→16.47 ms, −20%, manifests byte-identical; tree numbers reproduced by two independent implementations). Provenance: initially committed by a worker outside the coordination tree; see campaign log. (S2, adopted) writeManifest no longer pumps a fresh createReadStream per file: each of the 8 workers reuses one 1 MiB buffer over an explicit pread loop (short read = EOF, fd closed in finally). The stream machinery — not SHA — was the cost. Manifest output byte-identical, order unchanged, 8 MiB read cap unchanged. (S1, numbers-only) Big-fixture bill of health: on a 44.7 MB / 561-entry magazine the streaming thunk path peaks at 69–70 MB RSS vs 113 MB for the eager path and a ~57 MB theory floor — the 12 MB above floor is transient deflate/string churn the allocator retains, not a retained reference; no adoptable fix in src/epub.mjs. (S3, considered-not-adopted) downloadCover buffers (~1.6–6.4 MB transient incl. a failed JSON.parse of binary); <10% of process RSS, and the real win (hash-while-streaming into known) needs an archive-read + API change — owner lane. (S4) storage numbers below for owner decisions.

tradeoffs: hwm 4 MiB and 16 workers were measured and rejected: 4 MiB buffers made it WORSE (51.6→84.5 ms / 272→478 ms — a fresh 4 MiB alloc per read), 16 workers ≤−7.5%
per-worker pread holds one fd per worker concurrently (8) — same as the streams it replaced
the sync floor (readFileSync+hash) still beats the async path ~1.8–2× in microbench, but blocking the event loop during a CLI manifest pass is the wrong trade for a library function

the alt lane’s receipt (perf/lanes/T2-W2D-alt/) rejected only the hwm/worker KNOBS and never tested the pread algorithm — no contradiction with this adoption; its clean-bill RSS numbers (42.5 MB fixture, 1 ms RSS polling) are preserved as a second measurement

waves.name: Storage accounting — DECIDED by owner: EPUB-only readables
waves.change: Measured on the 44.7 MB magazine fixture: (a) the assembled EPUB contains 96.8% of the loose content bytes — each readable archive stores its book content ~1.97× (~88 MB on disk for a 45 MB magazine) because pages/*.xhtml + assets/* are kept alongside the EPUB that embeds them. The loose copies are the assembly source-of-truth and human-inspectable by design, so dropping them is a product decision, not a perf call. (b) Compact sidecar JSON would save 45% on thunder.json but 2.6 KB absolute, and −1% on openbook — rejected; human-readable archives are a product goal. — Owner decided (2026-09-09): go EPUB-only, conditional on zero data loss. Implemented as T2-W3 below. The sidecar-format question stays rejected (pretty-print kept).

metrics.name: readable folder size vs EPUB-only
metrics.unit: MB total on disk for a 45 MB magazine (~1.97×)

tradeoffs: decision question (a): keep pages/assets as the inspectable source of truth, or keep EPUB-only and re-derive pages on demand? Confidence: high on numbers, low on what the owner wants — implementation intentionally NOT started
decision question (b): none — compact sidecars are not worth it at these absolute sizes
waves.verified: numbers from perf/ram-big-one.mjs on the deterministic 45 MB fixture; notes in perf-notes-t2-ram.md

waves.name: EPUB-only readable archives (owner decision, lossless)
waves.change: Readable archives no longer keep loose pages/, assets/, or cover.jpg — the assembled EPUB is the archive’s single copy of the content. During the run, payloads stage in a per-run temp dir (os.tmpdir) so the disk-backed entry thunks are preserved: whole-book residency stays out of memory exactly as W16 designed, and the staging dir is deleted in a finally after assembly (invisible to the manifest walk; a crash mid-run can only orphan it in OS tmp, never inside the archive). Losslessness is pinned by e2e: assets and the cover are byte-identical inside the EPUB; each page’s decoded body is embedded verbatim inside the standards-required XHTML shell (wrapPage = fixed prefix + body + suffix — nothing removed, recoverable by unwrapping; the test pins the exact template so any change is a conscious decision). README.txt/README.md document the new layout.

metrics.name: readable archive at real scale (45 MB magazine, from T2-S4 fixture math)

tradeoffs: content inspection now needs an unzip (documented in README.txt); loose pages were a convenience, not a distinct artifact
page bodies are verbatim-but-wrapped inside the EPUB (raw-body recovery is deterministic unwrapping, not a file copy) — the byte-identical loose copy is gone by design
a kill mid-run can orphan a staging dir in OS tmp (never in the archive); there was no page resume logic before, so no capability is lost
RAM unchanged by design (staging preserves the thunk mechanism; ram-thunk tests pin it); W2C’s read-path pre-hash would have been partly obsoleted, but that bundle was already declined
audiobooks untouched: MP3 parts stay loose (no container holds them)
waves.verified: npm test 80 pass / 0 fail (e2e lossless assertions incl. byte-identity via unzip -p); coordinator measured old-vs-new folders via the sim harness; Safari report repointed to this worktree
